public_rationale: The research supports the ordinary, class-level reading: LLMs had disclosed verified personal information, researchers identified continuing underlying vulnerabilities, and the January legal evaluation found serious hallucination problems. A reported patch to the particular word-repetition attack limits the finding but does not establish a general solution. Support depends on reading private data to include personal information recovered from training data, rather than exclusively confidential conversations.
limitations: The extraction experiments preceded the target period; the contemporaneous outcome evidence concerns the continuing vulnerability assessment.
Personal information recovered from public-source training material is not necessarily secret information.
Legal benchmark error rates cannot be generalized to every LLM task.
The patch report is secondary reporting.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs sometimes leak private data, an unresolved problem, and hallucinations remain problematic.

statement.excerpt: It has become apparent that large language models, OpenAI’s core technology, sometimes leak private data, and that this problem has not been resolved; hallucinations too remain problematic.
statement.document_title: OpenAI’s Got 9.9 Problems, and Twitch Ain’t One

from_speaker: this problem has not been resolved
our_interpretation: The claim concerns persistent classes of LLM failure, not every model or every interaction.

Private data is read as personal or sensitive information disclosed through model output, including memorized personal information originally collected from public sources. Confidential user conversations are a narrower category.
Unresolved means the underlying disclosure risk remained, even if a particular extraction technique was blocked.
Problematic hallucinations means material factual errors in consequential uses, without imposing a universal error-rate threshold.
For the ongoing observation, use the latest completed quarter and the elapsed publication quarter: October 2023 through January 27, 2024.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous research establishes continuing personal-data disclosure vulnerabilities and material hallucination problems, while distinguishing individual mitigations from a general solution.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable evidence establishes that either asserted ongoing problem had been comprehensively resolved for the relevant LLM class during the target period.

evidence.excerpt: We recover personally identifiable information of dozens of individuals.
evidence.locator: Section 5, Qualitative analysis, PII; Ethics & Responsible Disclosure
evidence.explanation: The researchers verified extracted personal information against their comparison dataset. The attack was discovered and disclosed before the target period, so this is background evidence rather than a newly dated extraction outcome.

evidence.excerpt: language models are subject to divergence
evidence.locator: Patching an exploit != Fixing the underlying vulnerability
evidence.publisher: Authors of Scalable Extraction of Training Data from (Production) Language Models
evidence.explanation: This is the researchers’ dated assessment of the continuing vulnerability, not a claim that their experiments occurred on publication day. They explain why a word-repetition filter would address one exploit without eliminating memorization and divergence.

evidence.publisher: Dahl, Magesh, Suzgun and Ho, arXiv
evidence.explanation: The January assessment reports legal hallucinations ranging from 69% for ChatGPT 3.5 to 88% for Llama 2 on the specified questions. The date identifies the published assessment of the problem; the abstract does not specify individual test dates.

evidence.excerpt: OpenAI has been notified and the attack no longer works.
evidence.locator: Paragraph discussing OpenAI notification and the patch
evidence.explanation: This materially limits any assertion that the original ChatGPT exploit remained usable. The same report distinguishes that mitigation from resolving the underlying vulnerabilities.
